prompt: Our OrderService has three if-statements on payment type. Tests pass and it reads fine. Should I introduce Strategy plus a factory and registry now, just to be safe?

checks.name: advises-against-now
checks.pattern: leave (it|this|the code)( alone| as[- ]is)|(don'?t|do not|no need to|not worth|wouldn'?t|i'?d (not|skip))[\s\S]{0,40}(introduc|add|adopt|refactor|use strategy)|keep (it|them|the (if|code))[\s\S]{0,20}(as is|simple|for now)|not (yet|now)|hold off|premature

pass: No. Three branches that read fine with passing tests is not pain. Leave it alone until you have concrete evidence it is hurting you.
I wouldn't add a Strategy, factory and registry yet. That is premature without a measured problem; keep the ifs and revisit if a fourth type arrives with real bugs.
fail: Yes, Strategy with a factory and registry is the clean way to handle payment types. Here is how to set it up.
It depends. Strategy is a good pattern for payment handling and would make the code more extensible.
